lead_review: Approved explicit global --no-lazy-fetch in addition to env1, with unsupported Git failing closed.
source_state: Two source files modified after the fe24 retrieval checkpoint; exact hashes below. No application, corpus, ranking, fixture or manifest change.
problem: The custody helper promised local-only Git object reads, but an actual blob:none promisor checkout caused Git to fetch missing immutable evidence objects implicitly. This was a custody/acquisition contract defect, not an evidence byte mismatch.
correction: Both subprocess paths use git --no-lazy-fetch and force GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. Missing or malformed blob headers and nondecimal ls-tree sizes refuse before reconstruction. Preparation is a separate explicit operation. Unsupported older Git fails closed.

independent_review.receipt_source: Specialist A direct source review and independently executed actual disposable promisor controls, communicated 2026-11-26; retained here at reviewer request.
observations: Both Git subprocess paths, including extraction, force the offline boundary even when caller environment sets lazy fetching to zero.
Global --no-lazy-fetch makes unsupported older Git refuse rather than silently ignore an environment setting.
Malformed header shape and nondecimal size refuse before destructuring or conversion.
Actual file:// unguarded control fetches a promised blob; guarded controls issue no child fetch; explicit targeted preparation restores successful exact local reads.

explicit_preparation.scope: Only missing blob IDs enumerated from the predecessor custody manifest; no branch/ref/ancestry or checkout payload expansion. Original full evidence remains in its predecessor lineage.

qualification_limits: Four tests use an actual local file:// promisor transport in disposable directories, not an external GitHub outage simulation.
Complete predecessor verification reads actual locally prepared objects and compares manifest digests; it does not claim the compact branch erases historical Git storage.
No new remote host, credential, LFS policy or retrieval method is introduced.
